tools.name: resolve_package
tools.description: Resolve a package name plus exact version, dist-tag, or semver range to the version that exists on npm today, with its browser entry points. Use this instead of recalling versions from memory.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List the real files inside an exact or resolvable package version via UNPKG ?meta. Use this before choosing a file path; never guess paths.

tools.name: build_file_url
tools.description: Build a direct UNPKG file URL (the original file lookup) with a deliberate version policy, verifying the file exists when a path is given.

tools.name: audit_dependencies
tools.description: Classify a project's runtime dependencies for conversion to direct UNPKG file lookups, in framework context when given. Read the project's package.json yourself and pass its dependencies map; this tool checks each package against live npm/UNPKG data and returns convert_now / convert_carefully / keep

tools.name: verify_url
tools.description: Check that a UNPKG file URL actually resolves (follows redirects) before you put it in a project.

tools.name: generate_importmap
tools.description: Resolve a set of bare specifiers to UNPKG file URLs and return a ready-to-paste import map. Entry files are resolved live from each package.

tools.name: check_importmap
tools.description: Validate an existing or proposed import map: every UNPKG URL resolves, files exist, versions are mutually consistent (including react/react-dom pairing and duplicate-version skew), loose specs are flagged, and framework-managed packages are errors when a framework is given or detected. Run this afte

tools.name: search_packages
tools.description: Search npm for a need (e.g. 'date picker', 'markdown parser') and annotate each result with browser readiness for direct UNPKG file lookup: browser-ready ESM, CommonJS-only, or unclear, with the entry file and size when known. Ranking is npm's relevance order; readiness is annotated, never hidden, s

tools.name: estimate_migration_impact
tools.description: Order-of-magnitude estimate of bandwidth offloaded (and hosting dollars, if a $/GB is given) when bytes move from first-party hosting to UNPKG. Range-based with explicit assumptions and caveats; it cannot forecast latency or Core Web Vitals. Get unpkgBytesPerPageLoad from audit_dependencies' impact.

tools.name: shield_whoami
tools.description: Return the Shield account, organization, and entitlements for the OAuth login on this connection. Requires an approved Shield account; anonymous connections get an authorization_required error with reconnect instructions.

tools.name: shield_simulate_request
tools.description: Preview what Shield would do for one package@version request (optionally with referer/origin) under the logged-in user's effective pin/block rules, using the same rule-matching semantics as the edge.

tools.name: shield_check_packages
tools.description: Check exact package@version pairs against Shield intel: malware verdict (with review state) and CVEs affecting that version, including the first patched version. Works anonymously for packages you name (25 per call); Shield login raises the cap to 200. Domain data still requires login. Missing pairs

tools.name: shield_domain_packages
tools.description: List the caller's verified domains with package counts, or the packages Shield has observed on one domain. With includeThreats, one domain's packages come back annotated with malware verdicts and CVEs, ranked by the domain's own traffic. Requires Shield login.

tools.name: shield_watchlist_status
tools.description: Return the logged-in org's monitored packages, blocklist entries, and pin policies as Shield currently holds them. Requires Shield login.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "list_files" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "audit_dependencies" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Classify a project's runtime dependencies for conversion to direct UNPKG file lookups, in framework context when given. Read the project's package.json yourself…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "audit_dependencies" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "search_packages" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.detail: Description of "shield_whoami" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.
